excerpt: A non-resident's guide to buying Dubai property: designated ownership areas, documents, remote representation, registration and total cost.
introduction:
A non-resident can explore buying eligible Dubai property, but the right available depends on the property and the buyer's circumstances. Confirm the exact unit and ownership right with Dubai Land Department (DLD), verify the seller or developer, and plan how identification, funds and registration will be handled.

You do not need to assume a particular residence or visa outcome to compare a property purchase. This guide describes a practical sequence and points to official services; verify current requirements for your transaction before paying.
takeaways: Ask DLD to confirm the right available to you for the exact property in a designated area.
DLD's completed-property service lists a valid passport for non-resident foreign individuals.
Confirm representation, payment, registration, financing and tax implications for your own circumstances.

sections.heading: Where can a non-resident buy?
sections.body:
DLD's [frequently asked questions](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/frequently-asked-questions) explain that property for non-UAE citizens can be registered in areas designated under Dubai's real estate registration framework. The exact right and eligible area should be checked for the individual property; do not assume that every Dubai listing has the same ownership status.

Ask for the unit number, building, registered owner or developer and the nature of the right being offered. Compare the title or initial registration and plan with the sale documents. Verify the seller's authority, any mortgage or lease, and whether developer clearance is required.

The [JVC and Arjan area guide](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) provides a starting point for two Dubai communities, but it is not an ownership confirmation for a specific apartment.

rows: Designated area, exact unit and type of registered right
Current passport and any documents requested by the service
Valid authority, attestation and permitted signing scope
Payment channel, bank requirements, exchange costs and source documentation
Applicable DLD service, current fees and issued document

sections.heading: Prepare identity and representation documents
sections.body:
For a completed-property sale, DLD's [property sale registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/) lists a valid passport for non-resident foreigners and a developer e-NOC for applicable freehold areas. The documents can differ for a company, representative or another transaction type. Ask the service centre and relevant parties for the current list.

If you cannot attend, seek advice about a power of attorney or other authorised representation. Confirm the wording, notarisation, attestation, translation and validity requirements with the relevant authority before relying on a document signed abroad. Grant only the authority needed and verify the representative independently.

A passport, signed offer or agency agreement alone does not transfer ownership. Obtain and retain the official registration outcome for the property.

sections.heading: Plan the money and the actual cost
sections.body:
Arrange a traceable payment route and discuss banking, source-of-funds documentation, currency conversion and transfer times with your bank in advance. Verify payment instructions through independently confirmed contacts. Never assume a personal bank account is an appropriate recipient for an off-plan instalment.

Add the price, applicable DLD and service partner fees, agreed brokerage, legal or representation costs, financing charges and initial work. DLD's sale service lists 2% of the sale value for each party, though the agreement may allocate the total differently. Request an itemised quote and confirm who pays each amount.

For a simple worked example, a cash buyer pays AED 1,000,000 for a property and assumes AED 40,000 of combined transaction and setup costs. The initial outlay is AED 1,040,000 before an additional reserve. The AED 40,000 is the example amount for acquisition costs; use the applicable charges for your purchase.

chart.title: Example cash purchase before a separate reserve
chart.note: Sample inputs total AED 1,040,000. Use this worked calculation to organise the price and transaction costs for your own purchase.

sections.heading: Ready and off-plan checks differ
sections.body:
For a ready home, inspect the actual unit and common areas or appoint a qualified person to do so. Review the title, seller authority, service-charge statement, mortgage and tenancy. Confirm the transfer, settlement and handover sequence.

For off-plan, ask for the registered project and developer, contract, payment schedule, completion provisions and project payment details. DLD's [project registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-project) describes project registration and an escrow account for off-plan sales. Confirm the current details independently with DLD and the appropriate bank before transferring funds. Review the handover and payment terms alongside the safeguard provided by the escrow account.

Ask how the initial sale is registered and how you will receive evidence of that registration. Keep the contract, receipts and correspondence in one place.

sections.heading: Consider finance, tax and later management
sections.body:
If you need a mortgage, ask lenders whether they serve non-residents and what documents, valuation, deposit and terms apply. Approval, interest rate and maximum financing depend on the lender and your circumstances. Make a plan for a lower-than-expected loan or a delayed approval.

Consider reporting and tax obligations in the countries relevant to you with an appropriately qualified adviser. A Dubai purchase does not automatically settle obligations elsewhere. If you plan to rent the apartment, budget for building charges, vacancy, insurance, repairs and a licensed manager's fee.

A property purchase is also separate from a residence or visa application. Check current eligibility and documentation with the relevant official authority rather than assuming ownership automatically grants a visa.

sections.heading: Plan ownership administration from abroad
sections.body:
Ask how notices, service-charge statements and registration documents will be delivered after purchase. Keep your contact information current with the relevant parties and confirm how a representative may act if a repair or tenant issue arises while you are abroad. A management agreement should define spending limits, reporting and access to records.

Budget for international transfers and exchange-rate movement if your income is in another currency. These costs depend on your bank and transaction timing. Consider how quickly funds can be moved if an instalment, building charge or unexpected repair falls due.

sections.heading: Request a current shortlist
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your nationality, budget, intended use and whether you need remote representation. Ask which exact units are currently available and request their documents and written costs.

Verify the ownership right, official process and payment details independently before committing.
